## Product invariants
- Six fictional crew; every generated observation has `synthetic: true`, seed, scenario and generator version. Never claim live NASA medical data.
- Deterministic, quality-gated personal-baseline detection owns alerts. Language models and retrieval cannot create an original alert, change telemetry or prescribe treatment.
- Gray means missing, stale or unreliable. No numerical fallback may turn missing data into a healthy value.
- Every highlighted body domain needs measured evidence. The twin is a visualization, not a physiological simulation or anatomical diagnostic asset.
- Earth views show only delivered packets; preserve observation, transmission and receipt times. Blackout preserves outbound cases across restart. Human acknowledgement precedes case transmission.
- Local monitoring and local knowledge must work without external Internet. Renderer or retrieval failure must not stop monitoring.
- All authorization belongs on the server. No secrets in source, URLs, browser storage or logs. Demo identity selection is allowed only in explicitly local demo mode.

## Permanent visual design directive
- Apply [docs/VISUAL_DESIGN_SYSTEM.md](docs/VISUAL_DESIGN_SYSTEM.md) to every upcoming frontend and 3D module. ASTRA must feel like a premium cinematic deep-space mission-control environment, with a coherent identity across every screen. Avoid generic AI SaaS dashboards, default component-library aesthetics and generic dashboard templates.
- Primary backgrounds: near-black, void black, obsidian and graphite. Use layered charcoal surfaces, smoky glassmorphism, subtle translucent panels, refined borders, cinematic lighting, premium spacing and purposeful depth.
- Reference palette: Void Black `#050508`, Obsidian `#111116`, Graphite `#24242C`, Solar Amber `#F3A64A`, Nebula Violet `#9875E8`, Aurora Teal `#54C9B7`. Use restrained amber/violet/teal accents and occasional warm white highlights. Avoid generic blue dashboards, bright blue gradients, excessive cyan glow and repetitive neon cards.
- Reserve red for critical warnings, amber for caution, green/teal for healthy states and neutral gray for missing or unreliable data. Keep actual monitoring availability and risk severity distinct from decorative accents and from each other; include readable text/icons rather than color alone.
- Typography must be elegant, futuristic and readable, with clear hierarchy. Prioritize functionality, legibility, accessibility, responsive layouts and performance over decoration.
- 3D direction: immersive rotating Earth with atmospheric glow and realistic lighting; interactive astronaut twins with holographic anatomical styling. Preserve evidence-linked visualization and never invent pathology or health readings.
- Motion direction: smooth scroll-driven transitions, parallax, subtle particles, depth effects, responsive micro-interactions and premium camera movement. Keep motion purposeful and restrained; avoid distracting animation.
- Use GPU-efficient rendering, adaptive quality, graceful fallbacks and reduced-motion support. Preserve monitoring functionality and clear status through renderer or animation failure.
- Label synthetic telemetry clearly. Never display false live NASA data or let cinematic styling imply verified scientific capabilities.
- These are permanent design constraints, **not approval to implement upcoming modules or expand N03**. The original visual directive authorized documentation only; subsequent explicit approval authorizes bounded N03 correctness work. Preserve the single-module approval workflow; N04 and later modules require separate approval.
